- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.4) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast to reflect risk premium.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior day), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above prior peak.
- When sentiment turns sharply positive after a dip, model may lag; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% of recent range.
- If model shows steady upward trend with no volatility in sentiment, true price often reverses; apply mean reversion by subtracting 1–3% from forecast.
- In low-sentiment, flat-history periods, model tends to underestimate; add 2–5% to forecast to account for hidden risk or supply shock.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome deviates >10% from model, check sentiment history for recent divergence; if sentiment is neutral or negative, adjust downward.
